bears_on.note: Both ways: our extractors without turrets died to single Rovers from 2:34, and his naked greedy expansion lost six extractors and a constructor to three Rovers and one Blitz by 4:59.

Our first handful crossed (Blitz 2:10, his first extractor dead 3:02 against the pool median 2:48) and paid. His handful crossing the other way did the same to us. Scope: the crossing needs a picket at home (a turret) beside it, or it trades evenly.

In part: three of our Rovers on rove, with no special micro, killed six extractors and a constructor against a greedy opener's naked spots. The lesson's 'need specific micro to be worth anything' was said of a Rover mass against a guarded opening.
Extractors decided it: we never held more than 8 (2 at 5:00, 3 at 8:00), against his sighted 9+ at 7:47, 11 at 9:43 and 16 at 13:25; the armies traded about evenly 6:30-9:21.

The commander held the body home 4:47-10:13 on '8 extractors first' with his plant seen unturreted at 4:09, but the army lead was a floor of what was in sight. The commander read 'even, about 1,000 a side' at 7:47.
'less groups': the hands split the Blitzes into groups named A to B2, with 17 instructs 6:30-9:15 re-joining them.
Bombers struck at 11:15 with no anti-air standing (first Nettle 11:48, 1,495 lost); his air plant was never scouted.
An extractor in the plant's exit lane held Blitzes and constructors 30 s at a time (6:24, 10:44, 12:39). This is the defect fixed 2026-10-13 (3aabc77).

Three solars, then the plant's first unit a constructor at 1:12, the intent the lesson names; energy was still empty at 1:31 (13/1300), after which the game was metal-bound with energy full from 3:00.
The commander's 7:47 'eat the wrecks at G1' lifted metal income to 49 at 9:00, but the wrecks known at 12:00-14:00 (1,883 to 3,878 metal) were not being worked at the minute marks.
Turret frames competed with the plant under a metal store at 0 (2:37-8:00) before the priority flag existed. Reader's reading.

lens.caveats: No truth file, no results.jsonl, no batch.json: his numbers are floors of what we saw, and the loss and minute are inferred. pro_baseline needs --all-starts (no carded G1 Armada side) and prints '-' for our pressure rows although the record has the crossing at 2:10 and the first kill at 3:02. minutes.py guesses his start at B5 (his base was A8). analyze_match prints 'opponent None; outcome None'. floor.py has no result, known% or look_min. raid_ledger's 'paid' is 0 on every row for want of a truth file. None of the tools reads commander.jsonl (read directly). The existing review (Fable 5.1, 2026-10-04) ranks the same root; I differ in four places. (1) The 6:00-9:00 '2.2-9.3x' is a sight floor: engagements #1-#4 traded 1,485 for 1,272 and the commander read 'even' at 7:47, so I rank the hold below the defence chain, with the user. (2) At 2:02-2:34 the commander was there and the hands chose its list. (3) The trade was near level at 5:00. (4) The 5:17 stop of the plant turrets. The ledger's row says 'as the first' game, whose row says we were Cortex; this record says armcom (Armada). The existing review's 'no line in docs/experiments.md' is out of date (rows 676-677 now exist).

Was there a real army lead at 6:00-9:00? minutes.py's 2.2-9.3x counts only what was in sight at each sample, while the commander read the armies even at 7:47 and the fights then traded evenly.
Would the post-2026-10-17 hands have sent the commander's D-gun at the lone Rover at 2:26-2:34, and the whole body rather than hunts of one or two at 6:30-9:00?
Is a re-sent produce list still restarted from its head?
Which faction did we play in the first human-23 game? The ledger says Cortex for it and 'as the first' for this one, but this record is Armada.
